outcome: denoising and segmentation effect of dual-domain image denoising (DDID) algorithm
cohort: The study included 40 primiparas recruited from a hospital between January 2018 and January 2020, divided equally into a caesarean section group and a vaginal delivery group.
finding: The optimized DDID algorithm demonstrated superior denoising and segmentation effects for MRI images, and the incidence of pelvic organ prolapse (POP) was significantly higher in the caesarean section group (45%) compared to the vaginal delivery group (25%).
mod_finding: The incidence of pelvic organ prolapse (POP) was significantly higher in the caesarean section group (45%) compared to the vaginal delivery group (25%), with a P<0.05 difference.
